title: MLB trade deadline Big Board 2.0: Top 75-plus players ahead of Aug. 3 deadline
author: Tim Britton
content:
Just 14 days separate us from the Aug. 3 trade deadline, and we’ve yet to see a major pennant-altering blockbuster. No, Eric Lauer to the Dodgers for everyone’s favorite player, cash considerations, doesn’t count.

Consider the lack of movement a byproduct of the expanded playoffs, wherein there are three wild-card spots available in either league, and the Aug. 3 date, the furthest it can be under the current collective bargaining agreement. In other words, no one is truly out of it, and Aug. 3 might as well be Dec. 31.

At some point, action is expected to pick up, which is where we come in.

Welcome to The Athletic’s MLB trade deadline Big Board, a collection of 78 players who could move in the next two-plus weeks. This is the second of three Big Boards we’ll publish between now and Aug. 3.

A few things have changed since our last Big Board. We’ve removed Byron Buxton, Sandy Alcantara and Jeremy Peña, all of whom are unlikely to be dealt by their respective teams. We’ve also added several new names, including Kevin Gausman, Spencer Jones and Eugenio Suárez.

Not every player on this list will be dealt, and as was the case last year with Mason Miller going from West Sacramento to San Diego, there are inevitably going to be players we didn’t foresee being dealt actually being traded.

Also, including Jones doesn’t necessarily mean the Yankees will deal him, but it’s an acknowledgement that, as part of a potential larger package for one of the 77 other players, New York could find itself shipping him out.

Some bookkeeping: The player’s listed age is how old he is on July 15, B/T is the classic bats/throws, the money owed is via Baseball Prospectus and covers only the days after Aug. 4, the WARs from 2024 to present are updated through July 15, the WARs for ’26 are a projection from now until the end of the season. Both are from FanGraphs.

The likelihood of being dealt is a best-guess projection (from red as unlikely through yellow to green as likely), and the rankings are beyond reproach.
